articleTitle: LLM2AutoML: Zero-Code AutoML Framework Leveraging Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) aims to make machine learning accessible to non-experts by minimizing technical barriers and enabling the creation of high-performance models without extensive programming knowledge. Despite advances, existing AutoML solutions often struggle with complexity and inefficiency in handling intricate tasks. Herein, we present LLM2AutoML, a zero-code AutoML framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate high-performance actionable ML models without coding and with explanations. LLM2AutoML enables bidirectional human-machine alignment by interpreting user intentions expressed in natural language, converting them into executable AutoML tasks, and delivering detailed analytical reports that foster user understanding and trust. We propose the template-bounded AutoML method to ensure the LLM-generated code is highly executable, enabling fully end-to-end automation, including intention parsing, model auto-selection, and hyperparameter auto-tuning. Additionally, we incorporate techniques such as adaptive loss functions and configuration recommendations to improve efficiency and performance. Experiments on the SECOM dataset from the semiconductor manufacturing industry demonstrate that LLM2AutoML enhances the automation and usability of AutoML and LLMs, achieves superior performance, and produces high-quality analytical reports. This framework presents a novel approach to advancing the effectiveness and capabilities of both AutoML and LLMs.

articleTitle: Model-Based Position Control of Energy-Efficient Electro-Hydraulic Linear Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The rising interest in energy efficiency for hydraulic systems directs the research towards electro-hydraulic drives, namely linear actuators (i.e., hydraulic cylinders) directly coupled to pumps driven by electric motors. This approach removes functional power dissipations, enables energy recovery, and facilitates system commissioning. However, these drives are characterized by inherently low damping that causes unwanted payload oscillations and deteriorates the position control’s accuracy of the actuator. Adding active damping via proper control techniques is essential. Hence, this paper develops a model-based design for closed-loop position control with the addition of high-pass-filtered pressure feedback. The model supports identifying crucial control parameters, such as the proportional and integral gains of the position feedback and the gain and time constant of the pressure feedback. This method is experimentally tested on a heavy-duty robotic manipulator. The results show that the payload oscillations are reduced dramatically, and the position tracking is accurate and robust for different load cases.

articleTitle: The Artifact Removal Algorithm for EEG Based on Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) is easily contaminated by various artifacts, and many studies use the decomposition and blind source separation method to identify and remove artifact-related components. However, most studies using the threshold-based decomposition-blind source separation methods, leading to excessive suppression of brain activity and may not be able to remove specific artifact. Recently, self-supervised learning based on contrastive learning is developing rapidly and has achieved great success in the field of computer vision. At the same time, recent research shows that contrast learning can learn better representation with more generalization ability by comparing the pairwise distance within the feature space, and can achieve better results than supervised learning models after fine-tuning. In this study, an adaptive few-channel EEG denoising algorithm based on outlier detection was proposed. The potential components are extracted by blind source separation method, and the anomaly detection algorithm is used to identify the abnormal components according to the distribution of the components in the feature space. The entire process is completely data-driven and adaptive, so it is possible to remove a variety of different artifacts at the same time in a single session without over-inhibiting brain activity.

articleTitle: FuseGait: A Gait Recognition Network Integrated FuseFormer and Spatio Temporal Convolutions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Gait recognition (GR), a biometric identification method require no user cooperation, and operate unnoticed from a distance, making it an increasingly attractive area of research for both academia and industry. While the recent methods have achieved excellent results in controlled indoor settings, their performance deteriorates significantly in outdoor environments. Previous approaches have attempted to enhance performance by increasing network depth, but these methods eventually face limitations. Since gait is a behavioral biometric, temporal features play a crucial role in identifying individuals. To address these challenges, we propose a GR framework, FuseGait, which integrates long-term and short-term temporal features with multi-dimensional spatial features. Our FuseGait utilizes P3D-based residual network to establish localized spatiotemporal receptive fields and employs a multi-scale visual encoder to extract comprehensive spatial information. Furthermore, we utilize the FuseFormer block to capture the long-term temporal dependencies within silhouette sequences and fully integrate them with the convolutional branch. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on both indoor dataset (CASIA-B) and outdoor dataset (Gait3D).

articleTitle: Multi-Resolution Convolution for 3D Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Effective capture of multi-scale features is crucial for improving performance in 3D point cloud semantic segmentation tasks. This paper introduces a novel framework that enhances the extraction of semantic information from complex objects in 3D point clouds using multi-resolution techniques. By utilizing varying voxel resolutions and convolutional kernel sizes, we integrate high-resolution voxels to capture fine details and low-resolution voxels to extract global features, achieving robust feature fusion. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed network validated on the ScanNet v2 dataset, particularly excelling in the semantic segmentation task for small objects and complex scenes. This study highlights the significance of multi-resolution strategies in 3D scene understanding, providing new insights for future research in the field.

articleTitle: A Path Planning Method for Electric Vehicle Based on Q-Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has intensified the demand for efficient navigation methods to locate charging stations, optimizing both user convenience and energy utilization. This paper proposes a Q-learning-based path planning approach that dynamically identifies optimal routes for EVs while considering real-world constraints such as traffic and charging station availability. The proposed model integrates grid-based environmental modeling with reinforcement learning to achieve robust and adaptive path optimization. Experimental results, conducted on simulated urban environments derived from real-world data, demonstrate the algorithm’s ability to effectively navigate diverse scenarios, minimizing travel distance and avoiding obstacles. The findings highlight the potential of this approach to enhance EV navigation systems and lay a foundation for future research in high-complexity transportation networks.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Differential Privacy Scheme for Council Mechanism in Decentralized Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In the context of decentralized federated learning, achieving consensus and protecting data privacy are key challenges. In this environment, there is no central server, so a mechanism is needed to ensure that model updates from different participants can be securely and effectively aggregated. In this paper, we propose a privacy-preserving serverless federated learning framework—Adaptive Differential Privacy-based Committee Mechanism in Federated Learning (ADPCMFL), which aimed at addressing this challenge and achieving committee consensus. This scheme can dynamically adjust the degree of privacy protection based on the characteristics of data and learning needs, prevent inference attacks and Byzantine attacks, thereby improving the effectiveness and accuracy of learning while ensuring security and privacy. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed scheme in achieving committee consensus were verified through experiments and data analysis. Compared with existing methods, it can better balance privacy protection and learning performance, providing new ideas and methods for privacy protection and consensus building in decentralized federated learning.

articleTitle: System Identification Based Control Design for the Cart-Pole System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper presents a practical control approach for a cart-pole system, focusing on system identification, friction compensation, and rail limit management. First, a system model is developed, incorporating both kinetic and static friction effects. During the swing-up phase, system parameters are estimated to enhance control accuracy. An energy control method incorporating logarithmic barrier functions (LBF) is then used to swing the pole upright, ensuring the cart remains within the physical boundaries of the rail. Finally, a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) is designed to stabilize the pole in the upright position. All methods are validated on a real hardware system, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed parameter identification and control techniques in achieving stable and safe control of the cart-pole system.

articleTitle: Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty for Handwritten Digit Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) offers a powerful solution for generating high-quality synthetic data, addressing instability and mode collapse issues common in traditional GANs. This article explores the application of WGAN-GP in generating realistic handwritten digits using the MNIST dataset. WGAN-GP utilizes the Wasserstein distance metric rather than Jensen-Shannon divergence and introduces a gradient penalty to maintain the Lipschitz continuity constraint, which significantly improves training stability and image fidelity. We examine the effectiveness of WGAN-GP’s gradient penalty in preventing issues such as vanishing and exploding gradients, optimizing key hyperparameters, and enhancing the architecture for diverse and high-quality digit generation. Experimental results demonstrate WGAN-GP’s success in producing varied, lifelike handwritten digits and highlight the impact of key design choices, including latent space dimensionality and critic iterations, on image quality. Our findings suggest that WGAN-GP is a viable approach for applications requiring high-quality, synthetic digit datasets, potentially benefiting downstream supervised tasks in handwritten digit recognition and augmentation.

articleTitle: A novel dynamic robust control allocation algorithm based on second-order cone programming for tandem-wing UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dynamic robust control allocation algorithm based on second-order cone programming (SOCP) for tandem-wing UAV, with a focus on its application in reconnaissance-and-strike integrated missions characterized by high-dynamic, large-maneuver flight conditions. Leveraging the inherent flight control redundancy afforded by the aircraft’s unique aerodynamic configuration, the proposed method demonstrates enhanced robustness to uncertainties in the control efficiency matrix, in contrast to traditional methods such as the generalized inverse approach. The algorithm efficiently allocates control output of control rudders, minimizing deflection demands and ensuring stable control of the aircraft. The effectiveness of control allocation algorithms is rigorously validated through numerical simulations, confirming their superior performance and robustness in addressing the challenges of high-dynamic maneuvering flight.

articleTitle: An Improved Informed-RRT* algorithm for Mobile Robot Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Aiming at the limitations of the Informed Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (Informed-RRT*) algorithm in mobile robot path planning—specifically, its lack of goal orientation and directionality, inefficient searching, and lengthy planning times— this paper proposes an enhanced path planning algorithm that integrates the Artificial Potential Field (APF) method with the Informed-RRT* approach. Firstly, a probabilistic adaptive goal-biasing strategy is introduced to reduce search randomness. Secondly, the artificial potential field method is incorporated into the path extension process to reduce the required number of iterations. Additionally, a dynamic growth step size, based on obstacle density, is applied during the path generation phase to prevent local optima. Lastly, a bisection method is employed to create parent nodes, thereby enhancing path quality. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm significantly improves both efficiency and path quality over the standard Informed-RRT* algorithm.

articleTitle: The Application of GD-kWTA Network in Multi-Robot Competition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper applies the gradient-based differential kWTA (GD-kWTA) algorithm to multi-robot tracking tasks based on the principles of multi-robot competition and collaboration. At the same time, the kWTA network is modeled, and an activation function is added under noise-free conditions to improve the network's convergence speed. In the kWTA numerical experiment, special nonlinear activation functions are designed to activate the kWTA network to verify that the activation function has exponential convergence. Finally, under limited communication conditions, a consensus filter and the GD-kWTA network are combined as a robust control strategy to perform multi-robot target tracking tasks. At the same time, complex motion trajectories are set to further verify the effectiveness and reliability.

articleTitle: Prompting LLM for Embodied Tasks with Expert Instruction and Dimension Separation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: With the development of large language models, it has become possible to use multimodal models to build embodied agents. Currently, most approaches for handling embodied intelligence tasks with multimodal large models rely on prompt engineering or fine-tuning the models. However, to construct a general embodied intelligence model, the model needs to transfer world knowledge to corresponding embodied intelligence scenarios and spatial contexts. Language models that have not been optimized for embodied intelligence scenarios lack a good understanding of 3D scenes and the robot's action space. We attempted to address this issue in two ways, separated prompting approach where the model decomposes 3D spatial problems into 2D spatial problems and a trained expert model to guide the general model in spatial perception and action execution. Ultimately, the general model achieved improvements in embodied intelligence tasks. Experimental results demonstrated the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Target perception and grasping positioning system based on 2D-3D fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Accurate positioning of the target is the key to the robotic arm grasping task. However, due to the limitation of the hardware performance of the robotic arm, how to efficiently identify and accurately locate the target has become a major challenge, and the existing GPG grasping pose detection algorithm cannot be applied to the scene point cloud. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a target perception and grasping positioning system based on 2D-3D fusion. The system uses the YOLOv5 neural network for target recognition, combines NanoSAM to generate segmentation masks, and extracts the target's precise point cloud based on the results of the two, and inputs the GPG algorithm for grasping detection. Experimental results show that the positioning accuracy of this system exceeds 95%, and it shows good generalization ability on the Cornell grasping dataset, and can achieve efficient grasping and positioning in complex environments.

articleTitle: An Integral Enhanced Coevolutionary Neural Network Optimization Algorithm for Solving NonConvex Problem in Noisy Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper addresses nonconvex optimization problems in noisy environments by proposing an integral enhanced coevolutionary neural network (IECNN) optimization algorithm. The IECNN optimization algorithm integrates an integral enhanced recurrent neural network (IERNN) model with noise tolerance characteristics and an improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. It enhances global search capabilities and avoids local optima through adaptive inertia weight and stochastic mutation strategies. Experimental results demonstrate that the IECNN optimization algorithm performs excellently in solving the Griewank function and its application to angle-of-arrival localization problems. And it can obtain the optimal solution with fewer iterations and maintains high robustness and accuracy under various noise conditions.

Author Keywords: Integral enhanced coevolutionary neural network optimization (IECNN)

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Temporal Convolution Network for ERP Detection Based on an Auditory-Tactile Brain-Computer Interface System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: By delivering sensory stimuli in an oddball paradigm, the brain-computer interface (BCI) is able to capture subject’s electroencephalogram (EEG) signals and analyze it. While most P300-based BCIs rely on visual stimuli, prolonged visual attention may lead to fatigue and limit the applicability for patients with visual impairment. This study proposes a BCI system integrating spatial auditory and electro-tactile stimuli. The system employs a tailored Hierarchical Temporal Convolutional Network (HTCN) to improve the performance of event-related potential (ERP) detection. Six healthy controls were involved in BCI experiment for comparing different modalities, followed by exploratory BCI assessments with two visually impaired patients. Results show that healthy controls performed better in auditory-tactile (AT) modality than in auditory (A) and tactile (T) modalities, with an average online accuracy of 77.17% ± 4.84%. Furthermore, the designed HTCN achieved higher average offline accuracy compared to other approaches. These findings suggest that our proposed BCI system effectively enhances EEG effects in subjects, and it has potential in visual-independent clinical BCI assessment.

articleTitle: Key parameter design of wall pressing tracked pipeline robot under multiple constraint conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Wall pressing tracked pipeline robots have been widely used due to their high movement speed, strong drag force, and strong environmental adaptability. However, due to limitations such as pipeline diameter and shape, the design of their parameters has become a difficult problem. This article analyzes the design methods for the length, width, and head waist angle of a wall pressing tracked robot constrained by C-shaped and T-shaped pipelines. Firstly, based on the spatial position relationship of the wall pressing track pipeline robot in the C-shaped pipeline, flexibility and passability criteria are proposed based on the selection torque and movable space, respectively. Secondly, combined with the motion mode of multi-stage pipeline robots, the combination of actions through T-shaped pipelines was analyzed, and constraint equations were constructed based on spatial geometric relationships. Genetic algorithms were used to select key parameters of the robot. Finally, considering the constraint effects of C-shaped and T-shaped pipelines, the optimal parameters for robots that can pass through C-shaped and T-shaped pipelines are achieved. The robot and ground testing platform are processed, and the ground testing experiment is conduct. The test results show that the robot can pass through C-shaped and T-shaped pipelines well. The test results indicate that this design method is effective.

articleTitle: Research of Brain Controlled Lower Limb Rehabilitation Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Recently, lower limb exoskeleton robots have been widely used to assist stroke patients in completing lower limb rehabilitation training, and active rehabilitation training guided by patients' motor intentions can stimulate rehabilitation enthusiasm and improve training effectiveness. In order to achieve motion intention recognition and control lower limb exoskeletons to complete rehabilitation training, in this paper, a lower limb exoskeleton control method based on a brain computer interface based on motion imagery signals and lower limb joint angle gait data planning is proposed. Firstly, the common spatial pattern method is used to extract electroencephalogram (EEG) features, and convolutional neural network is employed to recognize motor intentions. Then, based on Fourier series fitting, the lower limb joint angle data is optimized to complete gait planning, and the lower limb exoskeleton is controlled to perform three training actions: walking straight, going up and down stairs. Finally, experiments on EEG recognition and exoskeleton control were completed. The results showed that the proposed method can recognize EEG signals and control the lower limb exoskeleton to drive the subject to complete corresponding rehabilitation training actions.

articleTitle: Design and experimental research of wave soldering electromagnetic pump
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Wave soldering machine driven by electromagnetic pump is the future trend. According to the structure of the wave soldering electromagnetic pump, based on the magnetic field calculation of the motor, the induced current and Lorentz force is caculated, and the flow rate and developed pressure model of the electromagnetic pump is established. On this basis, combined with the Bernoulli equation of fluid dynamics, wave crest height calculation model of wave soldering electromagnetic pump is constructed. Finally, the theoretical model is verified by experiment. The results show that: within the operating frequency range, the prediction error of crest height is about 12%, indicating that the model can provide a theoretical basis for the design of wave soldering electromagnetic pumps.

articleTitle: Review of Autonomous Driving in Unexpected Events
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In the field of autonomous driving, much of the research on decision-making systems focuses on predictable data. This paper emphasizes unpredictable data and behaviors, categorizing them into three types: (1) erratic behavior caused by issues with the driver, (2) behavior resulting from vehicle malfunctions, and (3) unpredictable driving behavior due to road conditions. Based on these categories, this paper establishes a database encompassing these three types of behaviors, which can be used to provide data for testing related algorithms. The analysis and research in this paper demonstrate that the ability of autonomous driving decision systems to assess unpredictable behavior is crucial for enhancing driver confidence and reducing traffic accidents.

articleTitle: Research on Robot Power Distribution Cabinet Operation Based on Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In recent years, the field of machine vision has developed rapidly, enabling the extraction of increasingly detailed information from images. At the same time, robotics technology has also advanced swiftly, with robots being widely applied in daily life. In our research, we combined machine vision technology with robotics to study operations for power distribution cabinets. Our system is based on a six-degree-of-freedom robotic arm, with the robot's end effector using a two-finger parallel electric gripper and an RGB-D camera for visual data acquisition. We also proposed a vision processing method to identify the status of the power distribution cabinet and to recognize and calculate the rotation angle of knobs. The system, utilizing these methods, was integrated into a power distribution cabinet platform for experimental testing. The robot was then controlled to perform the corresponding tasks, achieving success rates of 100%, 80%, and 70% respectively. Therefore, our proposed vision processing method effectively identifies and calculates the position and angle of buttons and knobs, and the integrated system successfully completed the corresponding tasks.

articleTitle: An Auditory Brain Computer Interface System Based on Naturalistic Paradigm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Naturalistic paradigms, which incorporate sensory stimuli commonly encountered in daily life, have garnered widespread attention in psychology and neuroscience in recent years. This study proposed an auditory brain-computer interface (BCI) system based on naturalistic paradigm. The system uses the reading of the article as a background while employing the sounds of chicken and dog as stimuli to evoke ERP from the subjects. To further enhance the performance of the BCI system, we improved the EEGNet model, which is based on convolutional neural networks, by incorporating a prototypical classifier to improve the classification performance in small-sample scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed paradigm with background evokes P300 components with higher amplitudes compared to the paradigm without background, thus improving the classification performance of BCI. Additionally, the modifications made to EEGNet further improved the model’s classification performance. Our proposed brain-computer interface system achieved an average online accuracy of 82.4% in eight participants, with five out of the eight participants achieving an accuracy of over 85%. The auditory BCI system proposed in this study may potentially assist patients with disorders of consciousness (DoC) in the future.

articleTitle: Human-machine shared control method for brain-controlled wheeled robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Human-machine shared control has been verified to be an effective method for brain-controlled robot. This paper proposes a shared control system for wheeled robots, which converts the EEG signals generated by SSVEP into the BCI command of the wheeled robot through vector fusion, and designs the RAC method to adjust the human-machine control weight based on the confidence evaluation of the EEG signals and the robot environment evaluation. Considering the problem of human-machine conflict, this paper adopts a "people-oriented" strategy and proposes the SCR-TEB algorithm to resolve human-machine conflicts. Online experiments have proved that the method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the success rate of the task and give people a stronger sense of control.

articleTitle: Using electrical stimulation to construct memories of specific area for robo-pigeon
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Robo-pigeon is a special robot that controls the behavior of a live pigeon by applying electrical stimulation to its brain nerve or muscle tissue. Currently, the predominant control methods for robot pigeons involve direct stimulation of the motor brain regions associated with movement to regulate their behavior. However, there is a deficiency in methods enabling pigeons to express their subjective movement inclinations and engage in activities within specific spatial confines. In this study, an experimental paradigm was designed to enable pigeons to generate spatial cognition and form memories of specific areas. Throughout the experiment, pigeons were positioned inside a specially marked circle. Whenever a pigeon attempted to depart from the circle, electrical stimulation was applied to its Formation reticularis medialis mesencephali (FRM) brain region. Experimental findings indicate that pigeons can develop a robust spatial memory of the marked area within approximately a week. Moreover, minimal stimulation can induce pigeons to move within a defined area. These findings have contributed significantly to the advancement of novel control methodologies for robot pigeons.

articleTitle: Lightweight Track surface defect detection method based on improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The detection of small and clustered defects in railway track surfaces remains a challenge due to the limitations in real-time accuracy of current methods. To address this, we introduce Ghost-YOLOv5-Rail, a novel algorithm based on YOLOv5, for defect recognition. A new dataset Rail-2k was developed to overcome data scarcity. The CBS and C3 modules in the backbone were replaced with GhostNet, and the ECA module was integrated into the C3 module to replace the SE module, forming the ECA-C3Ghost module to mitigate dimensionality reduction issues. Additionally, a CBAM attention mechanism was introduced in the NECK to enhance feature extraction. Comparative experiments demonstrate a 58.6% reduction in FLOPs (from 109.1 to 45.2), a 3.16% increase in mean average precision, and a detection speed of 80.6 FPS. These results highlight the potential of Ghost-YOLOv5-Rail to advance real-time track defect detection accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of the Manhole Cover Replacement Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of low efficiency and safety hazards in China's manhole cover management, this study created a novel kind of replacement equipment. To increase the speed and safety of replacing manhole covers, the gadget consists of an adaptable asphalt machine and a one-time forming manhole cover cutting machine.The cutting machine can automatically cut and replace manhole covers because it has cutting, moving, and magnetic mechanical arm functions that use machine vision to accomplish exact positioning. The adaptive asphalt machine optimizes the asphalt laying and compaction process and increases work efficiency by combining completely autonomous feeding and compaction components. This strategy addresses the growing issues of aging and labor scarcity, encourages the development of intelligent. This strategy encourages the development of smart cities, addresses the growing issues of aging and labor scarcity, and offers more trustworthy assurances for the safety of people' travels.

articleTitle: A gait planning approach for quadruped gecko like robots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: With the advancement of science and technology, the application fields of quadruped robots are gradually expanding. The core issue that needs to be addressed is to study and improve the motion mode in order to enhance the overall performance of quadruped robots. This article proposes an optimized triangular gait planning based on a specific gecko quadruped robot configuration. Triangular gait is widely used in hexapod robots, which enables the robot to maintain stability in complex environments, reduce energy consumption, and improve work efficiency. This article establishes a spatial coordinate system for the single leg of a quadruped robot using the D-H algorithm, and calculates the kinematic forward and inverse solutions of the single leg with given parameters. Afterwards, based on the above conclusions, design a single leg end trajectory to ensure that the foot movement trajectory is as smooth as possible. Finally, consider and calculate the overall center of gravity trajectory of the robot to comprehensively design the robot's triangular gait. The simulation results show that the foot trajectory design meets the design requirements, and the quadruped robot can achieve stable walking under the improved triangular gait.

articleTitle: Human-Machine Coupling Model Simulation for Wheelchair Posture Adjustment in OpenSim
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: To address the issues of insufficient comfort for the elderly and disabled when using wheelchairs, as well as the potential safety hazards associated with wheelchair posture adjustment experiments, this paper establishes a human-machine coupling model to study the interaction forces between human and wheelchair during the wheelchair posture change process. We collect experimental data on the movement posture and human-machine interaction forces as subjects passively transition from a sitting position to a lying position in a wheelchair. The wheelchair used in the experiments is modeled and simplified, and a coupling model of the human body and wheelchair is constructed within the OpenSim software environment. The collected data are tracked and simulated using Moco, and the simulation results are compared and analyzed against the experimental data. We verify the accuracy and reliability of the established human-machine coupling model.

articleTitle: X-Ray-Based Three-Dimensional Shape Reconstruction Method for a Continuum Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The utilization of visual sensors for three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction of continuum manipulators is a well-established technique, offering essential support for precise control and accurate state estimation. This approach has been widely adopted across various fields, including surgical robotics, bionic systems, and industrial automation. However, the effectiveness of visual sensors is substantially constrained in environments characterized by occlusions or spatial limitations, where accurate reconstruction becomes challenging. To overcome these limitations, we propose an advanced 3D reconstruction method leveraging X-ray imaging, enabling robust shape reconstruction and automated tracking of continuum manipulators, even under occluded conditions. In the X-ray-based 3D shape reconstruction method, the intrinsic and extrinsic parameters of the computed tomography (CT) device are calibrated. Besides, the X-ray images are processed with identification and segmentation, centerline detection and Bézier curve fitting. Finally, the 3D shapes of a continuum manipulator are accomplished by matching the two images acquired from two distinct CT device rotation angles and reconstruction. The measurement experiment has demonstrated the accuracy of 3D shape reconstruction achieved 0.5383 mm. The shape reconstruction experimental results also showed the effectiveness of the X-ray-based 3D shape reconstruction method.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Performances between Fuzzy and Fuzzy PID Temperature Controllers in Phototherapy Incubator for Infant Jaundice Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Fuzzy control demonstrates remarkable flexibility in addressing nonlinear issues and formulating algorithms through an if-then rule pattern. However, a fuzzy controller requires a substantial number of fuzzy grades, leading to increase many rules for achieving higher accuracy. This study introduces an efficient Fuzzy-PID (FPID) controller designed to manage the degree of membership in the fuzzy inference system, specifically for temperature control in a phototherapy incubator. Comparative analyses of the performance of the fuzzy and FPID controllers were conducted in a computer simulation. The FPID controller exhibited significantly superior performance, notably reducing the time delay compared to the fuzzy controller. In the simulation, the delays for the FPID and PID controllers were approximately 0.5 and 5 seconds, respectively. The equivalent fine-tuning of the PID controller for the fuzzy logic controller is straightforward to implement and offers high performance in regulating the temperature of the incubator. Consequently, the simulation results provide valuable insights for the design of modern phototherapy incubators used in the treatment of infant jaundice.

articleTitle: Tendon-Driven Anti-Fall Exoskeleton System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: To address the accidental fall when workers climb high-voltage towers, this paper designs a tendon-driven anti-fall exoskeleton system with the function of sensing and actuation. In the sensing part, the proposed device uses a hand pressure sensor combined with a classification algorithm to achieve a good classification effect, and can achieve an accuracy rate of 93% after data collection and annotation. In the mechanical design section, to determine the locations of anchor points, we use the finger model. Additionally, a motor-cable experimental platform is designed for the selection of a spool and test of system performance. Data collection and analysis are performed to establish the control logic. The experiments demonstrate that the system could provide 8.04 Ncm of finger joint torque within 0.2 seconds. The system can be used as a reminder during workers' climbing and significantly contributes to operational safety.

articleTitle: Visual servo assembly method for component docking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper adopts a spatial discretization model and grid model in traditional path planning methods to discretize the posture mechanism's workspace into a gridded array of positions with various posture angles. A collision detection model using octree segmentation is then applied to detect collisions and document the first safe posture encountered. This approach establishes an enhanced path planning method that separates collision detection and path planning, specifically designed for large component docking. It boosts posture adjustment efficiency while maintaining safe docking operations. Additionally, a visual servo posture control flow is proposed for large component docking based on a traditional servo control system model, introducing evaluation metrics and performance indicators. A visual-guided posture adjustment system is developed for ship sections and validated through experiments. The system architecture, hardware selection, and establishment are discussed in detail. Hand-eye calibration of the 3D camera is performed to unify the docking system's internal coordinate system. Path planning, posture adjustment, and visual-guided docking experiments are then conducted to verify the system's reliability under various poses.

articleTitle: Visual Exploration-Enhanced Quadruped Robot with Active-Passive Composite Telescope Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Navigating hazardous environments and confined spaces during disaster search and rescue operations poses significant challenges to both human rescuers and conventional robotic systems. Recognizing the need for enhanced capabilities, we introduce a Visual Exploration-Enhanced Quadruped Robot (VEQR), a novel platform specifically designed to improve adaptability and exploration in such demanding scenarios. The VEQR combines a quadruped robot with an innovative active-passive composite telescopic mechanism—a compact, 12.8 mm diameter device equipped with a camera—that enables maneuvering through narrow and curved spaces like slits and debris-filled areas. The bending and insertion/retraction capabilities of this mechanism improve the dexterity of the robot in confined spaces and extend its reach into deeper, hard-to-access zones. Experimental results demonstrate the VEQR’s proficiency in overcoming obstacles, inspecting confined spaces, and providing clear visual feedback. Notably, the VEQR successfully traversed narrow and winding passages as small as 50 mm diameter and inspected targets positioned up to 0.6 mm deep within confined spaces, confirming its effectiveness as a robust robot for search and rescue operations in hazardous environments.

articleTitle: Design and Validation of Discrete-Time Zeroing Neural Network for Time-Dependent Linear System of Equation and Inequality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In this paper, the discrete-time form of zeroing neural network (ZNN) is proposed and studied for the time-dependent linear system of equation and inequality (TDLS-EI). Specifically, the numerical difference formula based on Taylor series expansion is presented. Then, through utilizing the Talyor difference formula to discretize the existing ZNN model, a novel discrete-time ZNN (DTZNN) model is built to address the TDLSEI. Numerical simulation is implemented to verify the superior and effective performance of the proposed DTZNN model.

Author Keywords: linear system of equation and inequality

articleTitle: Research on Robot Motion Teaching Based on Human Pose Reconstruction Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The objective of this research is to explore a humanoid dual-arm robot motion teaching method that integrates human pose reconstruction technology, additionally, the study assesses the accuracy of the robot in replicating actions. Firstly, we employed an improved Denavit-Hartenberg (D-H) parameter method for kinematic modeling of the robot's configuration. Subsequently, we extracted motion data from various video sources using a human pose reconstruction model. After preprocessing the data, we optimized redundant degrees of freedom and applied the Jacobian iterative method for kinematic solving to replicate human actions observed in videos. Furthermore, we assessed the results of robotic action reproduction through two dimensions: positional error and action similarity. Experimental results indicate that the robot successfully reproduces various actions from different videos. However, factors such as video quality and background can affect model capture precision, thereby influencing the reconstruction effectiveness of certain movements. For humanoid-configured robots, after appropriate data processing, employing deep learning-driven human pose reconstruction algorithms enables rapid and cost-effective construction of a robotic motion library.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Fault Diagnosis of Control Valve
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Due to the distribution of control valves across different control loops within industrial systems, posing a significant challenge in collecting adequate fault data that covers various working conditions. Furthermore, industrial equipment often faces resource constraints when deploying data-driven models. To this end, a lightweight meta-learning fault diagnosis method is proposed to address the problem of few-shot fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions. First, to effectively address the unsteady time-varying fault signals, the two-dimensional (2-D) cloud model (CM) is employed to reconstruct the fault signals, thereby characterizing the states and features of the fault signals more comprehensively. Subsequently, a lightweight meta-learning model is constructed, the initial network parameters are randomly generated, and the parameters are updated by gradient descent. Finally, the parameters of the meta-learner are improved on the new task, and a few-shot data can be used to achieve rapid adaptation to new tasks. The experimental results show that the proposed method has significant advantages compared with other traditional meta-learning methods.

articleTitle: Research on deep neural network based classification method for social robots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: we propose a classification method for social bots in this paper. The microblog comment text topic is first extended so topic can express the event content more effectively. Then a generative adversarial network model is used to determine the relevance of the microblog text and the extended topic to detect contaminants. Then the social bot opinion sentence generation rule is combined with the deep learning model TextCNN to get the opinion sentence recognition method to further distinguish the commenters from the spreaders. Finally, migration learning is used to train the model to improve the classification effect.

articleTitle: Bolt identification and positioning method based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Prefabricated steel structure buildings are increasingly being applied in the construction of transmission towers, substation infrastructure projects, and main power plant buildings. Bolt is an important connection method in the connection process, and bolt tightening is an engineering problem that needs to be solved at present. There is an urgent need for the development of a bolt tightening robot specifically designed for steel structure connection nodes to address this issue. This paper focuses on the visual recognition and positioning technologies for such a robot, particularly the development and training of a deep learning model for bolt recognition, the acquisition of the bolts' three-dimensional coordinates within the camera coordinate system, and the real-time detection and feedback of coordinate information. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Predictability of Fault Events for Decentralized Stochastic Discrete-Event Systems Based on Dynamic Observations and Polynomial-Time Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Fault prediction of discrete-event systems (DESs) is to predict the fault prior to its occurrence such that effective measures can be taken. We investigate the issue of the fault copredictability of stochastic DESs (SDESs) in a decentralized setting under dynamic observations. It is supposed that the observation of events of the system is not fixed in advance. To perform the decentralized prediction of SEDSs, a D-coverifier from the given stochastic system with multiple local projections is constructed and a necessary and sufficient condition for the verification of D-copredictability by the D-coverifier is presented, which is polynomial-time complexity.

articleTitle: Investigation of wearable multi-sensor fusion monitoring system
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: To address the issue of falling risk during prolonged tower climbing for grid inspection, this paper presents the design of a wearable multi-sensor fusion monitoring system. The calibration experiment determines the fitting function between the digital quantity collected by the thin film pressure sensor and the applied pressure. A method for determining optimal hand sensor placement points is proposed based on a combination of average value and voting methods. Wearable data gloves and insoles are fabricated using sewing technology, and combined with a linear amplifier module, single chip microcomputer, and control terminal to form the wearable multi-sensor fusion monitoring system. To validate the reliability of the system, several climbing experiments were conducted. The experimental results demonstrate that the system can real-time monitor climbers' movement state and fatigue level, which is crucial for ensuring worker safety at high altitudes.

articleTitle: Face Expression Recognition Method Based on Mamba and Different Facial Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of information technology, facial expression recognition has become increasingly critical in various applications. To enhance recognition accuracy and computational efficiency, we propose a novel integration of the Vision Mamba framework with facial part-based image classification. This approach precisely segments key facial regions using Grad-CAM heatmaps, enabling the Mamba model to extract and analyze deep features from critical areas. By leveraging these techniques, our method achieves superior classification performance across multiple datasets. Experimental results demonstrate its robustness and efficiency, making it highly suitable for facial expression recognition. This work provides a practical and scalable solution, paving the way for advancements in intelligent systems and broader application scenarios, such as human-computer interaction and affective computing.

articleTitle: A Method for Suppressing Electrical Feed-through in Force-to-Rebalance Mode Hemispherical Resonator Gyroscopes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Hemispherical resonator gyroscopes (HRGs) are a type of solid wave gyroscopes with high precision and high reliability. The electrical feed-through from the driving signals to the detecting signals degrades the performance of HRGs severely. In this paper, the influence of the electrical feed-through induced by the amplitude control loop on the scale factor and the bias of the force-to-rebalance HRGs is theoretically analyzed. An automatic gain control (AGC) structure based on parametric excitation is proposed and demonstrated in a force-to-rebalance mode HRG. Experimental results reveal that, with parametric excitation, the electrical feed-through can be effectively suppressed, and the performance of the gyroscope was greatly improved.

articleTitle: Computer Vision-Aided Object Motion by Individual Cameras of Small-Sized Humanoid Robot: A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The small-sized humanoid robots (SSHR) have attracted considerable attention in research due to their affordability and versatility. The calibration method for the SSHR, Aelos (LeJu Company, China), employed in this study utilizes the black and white checkerboard drawing as the calibration object. The experimental outcomes are 19.57 ± 0.08 (20 cm), 24.59 ± 0.05 (25 cm), and 31.44 ± 0.06 (30cm) in the tests of the camera on the chest, as well as 29.60 ± 0.06 (30 cm), 34.59 ± 0.07 (35 cm), and 40.14 ± 0.07 (40 cm) for measuring the distance between the SSHR and the target. Moreover, under the circumstance of a simpler background of the picture, bounding the s ratio between 28% and 33% enhances the precision of the SSHR’s grasping at the center point of the sponge cube.

articleTitle: An Efficient Multi-Modal Image Registration Method for Intelligent Acupuncture Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This invention presents a multimodal image registration method for intelligent acupuncture robots, equipped with imaging devices such as the ultrasound and optical tracker. These multimodal images provide distinct information in various formats, but bring challenges for acupuncturists in image interpretation and processing. To address this, a multimodal image registration method is developed based on acupoint structure and acupuncture planning, aiming to align images of different formats to produce comprehensive images of acupoints’ epidermal surfaces. To enhance the accuracy of needle insertion monitoring and assessment, the proposed method employs rigid multimodal image registration, integrating ultrasound, optical tracking, and depth camera technologies. Given the point sets from ultrasound, optical tracker, and depth camera images, two rigid transformations map the ultrasound and optical tracker point sets onto the depth camera coordinate system. The rigid registration assumes a single transformation matrix for all points in the same image, optimizing alignment with the target point set. Since ultrasound provides 2D cross-sectional images and depth cameras and optical tracker yield 3D data. The method first positions the ultrasound’s 2D cross-section in 3D space using the needle insertion point and robot needle tip coordinates. Feature extraction from ultrasound images is followed by real-time matching and registration. Upon successful registration, the needle tip position is tracked across all modalities.

articleTitle: Application of stepwise regression method in aerodynamic parameter identification of unmanned aerial vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The system identification theory is an important tool for modeling vehicle dynamics. Aiming at the situation that the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) flight test conditions are limited and complete flight data cannot be obtained, a method for estimating aerodynamic angles and aerodynamic coefficients based on measurable data is proposed. Taking the flying wing UAV as an example, the aerodynamic parameters were determined and calculated by the stepwise regression method. The comparison of test data and simulation results verifies the correctness and practicality of the method. Considering the mathematical nature of discriminant modeling, the method is generally applicable to fixed-wing UAVs with various aerodynamic layouts.

articleTitle: OpenSim-Based Human-Robot Coupling Simulation of a Piggyback Nursing Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: To address the current issue of comfort lack in the piggyback nursing robot, the movement trajectory debugging is easy to cause secondary injuries to the care recipient, and the human-robot coupling research is insufficient, among other things. In this paper, a human-robot coupling model between the piggyback nursing robot and the human body is established by OpenSim, and the human-robot contact force during back-carrying movement is investigated. Firstly, the structure and function of the piggyback nursing robot are introduced. Based on this, a human-robot contact force testing experimental system is constructed, and the human-robot contact force during back-carrying movement is obtained through experiments. Then, human-robot coupling model is built in OpenSim. Finally, the human-robot contact force is obtained by simulating the robot back-carrying movement, and the validity of the human-robot coupling model is verified by comparing the experimental results of the human-robot contact force test. The analysis reveals that the axillary force has a greater impact on the comfort of the care recipient compared to the chest force, and excessive force in the Y direction is a major contributor to the sensation of compression.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional robust formation control for multiple uncrewed underwater vehicles based on Port-Hamiltonian theory under external disturbance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This article studies the formation control problem of multiple uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs) under time-varying external disturbances. The formation system is composed of a leader UUV and two follower UUVs. A three-dimensional (3D) formation robust control protocol of multi-UUV is presented based on the interconnection and damping assignment passivity-based control (IDA-PBC) method and the disturbance observer (DOB) technique. Firstly, the original UUV models are transformed into the Port-Hamiltonian (PH) structure. Next, the desired closed-loop PH system of the UUVs is constructed. With the IDA-PBC method, the design procedure of the formation controller is equal to solving matching equations, making the controller design intuitive. The DOB technique is introduced to compensate for the external time-varying disturbances to improve the robustness of the formation system. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed method accomplishes satisfactory formation performance and demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed control protocol.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Pest Count Forecasting for Solar Insecticidal Lamps
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Agricultural pests severely threaten food security, resulting in significant economic, social, and environmental impacts. This paper uses weather data and machine learning models to forecast pest counts. Data from solar insecticidal lamps, including pest counts and meteorological conditions, were collected. Using this data, we developed a multidimensional forecasting model. The model integrates crucial variables, including pest counts, temperature, humidity, and geographical coordinates. The genetic algorithm back propagation neural network model has demonstrated excellent performance in forecasting pest numbers, with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.73, confirming its effectiveness in the early detection of crop diseases and pest infestations. Moreover, this high-accuracy forecasting model provides a scientific basis for intelligently adjusting the insecticidal working time of solar insecticidal lamps, thereby enhancing pest control efficiency and energy utilization. This research not only reinforces the application of machine learning in agricultural pest management but also provides significant support for precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulations of Filtered Reciprocal-Kind Zhang Neural Network for Solving Time-Varying QP Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In our previous work [1], we introduced the filtered reciprocal-kind Zhang neural network (FRKZNN) model for handling time-varying quadratic programming (QP) problems. In this paper, we conduct two sets of numerical simulations to evaluate the model’s generalization, analyze the influence of its parameters, and perform an ablation study. The results from these simulations demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed FRKZNN model.

articleTitle: Autonomous Delivery Vehicle System Based on Multi-Sensor Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of science and technology, people's yearning for a more convenient life has gradually become concrete, which has given rise to a huge logistics industry chain. At the same time, the ever-increasing labor costs have caused an urgent need for autonomous delivery vehicles. This paper presents the design and integration of an autonomous vehicle system for efficient indoor parcel delivery, addressing the challenges of navigating dynamic indoor environments. This vehicle system leverages a multi-sensor approach, integrating LiDAR, radar, Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), GPS, and odometer data to provide comprehensive environmental perception and precise localization, which will contribute to the field by providing a practical application of autonomous vehicle technology in a constrained environment, offering a solution for the logistics industry’s indoor delivery challenges.

articleTitle: YOLOv10-Based Object Detection Method with Optimized Defogging Algorithm for Autonomous Driving in Foggy Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In foggy driving environments, the precision of object detection by autonomous driving systems is significantly diminished compared to clear weather conditions. To date, there is an abundance of work on object detection, yet research focusing on object detection in foggy scenarios for autonomous driving remains scarce. Firstly, due to the scarcity of publicly available datasets for vehicles in foggy conditions, this experiment constructs a foggy environment vehicle dataset. Subsequently, I integrated an enhancement module based on the NLD (Non-Local Image Dehazing) algorithm into the YOLOv10 model, yielding a new model capable of vehicle detection in foggy environments. Furthermore, I performed the same operation on various other YOLO models and conducted model evaluations. The results demonstrate that the new model, incorporating NLD, demonstrates a marked enhancement in object detection accuracy compared to the original models, enhancing the precision and robustness of vehicle detection in foggy conditions, thus offering greater application value in foggy autonomous driving scenarios. The foggy dataset for the experiment is available on GitHub: https://github.com/yiming676/Hazed-VehicleDataset.

articleTitle: Cooperative Co-evolutionary Genetic Algorithm for Generating Adversarial Examples
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Deep neural networks have rapidly advanced, with many models demonstrating outstanding performance. However, robustness is crucial for ensuring the safety and stability of artificial intelligence, especially in real-world applications where models are frequently exposed to interference. Research on adversarial example generation is significant for improving model robustness and preventing sensitive information from being interpreted. This paper proposes a Cooperative Co-evolutionary Genetic Algorithm (CCGA) for generating adversarial examples with small perturbations. The algorithm adopts a collaborative optimization strategy, demonstrating high efficiency when dealing with large-scale problems. Furthermore, it operates as a black-box attack method, requiring only access to the model’s inputs and outputs without any knowledge of its structure or parameters. Experimental results on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets show that CCGA achieves adversarial success rates of 97% and 100%, respectively, with mean squared errors as low as 7.41 and 12.00 between the adversarial and original samples, the differences are nearly imperceptible to human eyes.

articleTitle: A Cerebellar Model Articulation Controller Enhanced Neural Solution to Time-Varying Linear Equations With Robotic Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Time-varying linear equations (TVLEs) are common in practice. The existing TVLE solvers like the gradient-dynamics based neurodynamic networks (GDNNs) unavoidably introduce inevitable errors. In contrast, Getz-Marsden dynamic inverters (GMDIs) and error-dynamics based neurodynamic networks (EDNNs) require time derivatives of the coefficients and matrix inversion. To circumvent these limitations, a cerebellar model articulation controller (CMAC) enhanced GDNN (CMAC-GDNN) is proposed, where CMAC serves as a derivative estimator inspired by the fine-tuning correction mechanism for motion signals of the cerebellum. The CMAC-GDNN solver integrates GDNN and CMAC models that generate approximate solutions and correction signals, respectively. The CMAC-GDNN solver possesses some advantages of GMDI and EDNN solvers, avoiding complexities associated with the time derivatives and matrix inversion. In this paper, the structure of the CMAC-GDNN solver is presented in detail with its effectiveness and practicality demonstrated through a numerical example and a motion planning task in which a robot tracks a specific path.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of humanoid dexterous hand based on worm gear
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Humanoid robots have broad development prospects, and the global market size is expected to break through hundreds of billions of dollars, but the current humanoid robot market is still in the exploration stage. Dexterous hand as the end effector of robot and environment, is an important part of the development of intelligent humanoid robot, but dexterous hand in the realization of mass production, large-scale use of the road, there are still many problems to be solved. In this paper, aiming at the complex joint structure of humanoid dexterous hand, as well as the sliding and turning problems, combined with the analysis of the structure and function of the human hand, a five-finger dexterous hand based on worm gear structure is designed. It has the advantages of simple structure, saving the internal space of the hand and self-locking. The kinematic model of the dexterous hand is established by using solidworks. The dexterous hand consists of 5 fingers with the same structure and a palm. ADAMS software is used to create a virtual model of dexterous hand, and the grasping test and self-locking function verification of five-finger dexterous hand are carried out. The results show that the dexterous hand based on worm gear structure can be applied to the needs of daily life, industry and service industry.

articleTitle: 3D Path Planning Based on Dynamic Goal Bias and Critical Region Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper presents a path planning algorithm based on dynamic target bias (Bi), an improved artificial potential field (APF) model, and a critical region sampling strategy, referred to as the Bi-APF-RRT* (dynamically-target-biased artificial potential field and rapid random tree) algorithm, aimed at optimizing path planning in complex 3D environments. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms traditional RRT* and APF-RRT* algorithms in terms of both path length and smoothness. The dynamic target bias helps mitigate the local optimization problem inherent in traditional methods, while the improved APF model enhances obstacle avoidance and reduces path oscillations. The critical region sampling strategy improves the algorithm's adaptability and robustness, making these improvements particularly suitable for complex environments, such as autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Bipedal Walking Outdoors with a Point-footed Robot via Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The bipedal robot can perfectly adapt to the scenes of human society without the need for additional structural design and motion planning. Although model-based control algorithms achieve multiple types of motion, the control robustness is still insufficient in the face of complex dynamic environments. Reinforcement learning (RL) methods have recently produced good results in the field of bipedal robots. In order to explore information and exploit it better in the robot state space, we introduced a transformer structure that is more sensitive to temporal information into the RL framework. Benefiting from the self-attention mechanism in the transformer, our observation scheme extracts more state features, allowing the bipedal robot to achieve robust outdoor locomotion, including bipedal walking on asphalt, marble and grass terrains, including the test of performance on the most commonly used asphalt according to quantitative data.

articleTitle: A Novel Penalty Strategy Finite-Time Convergent-Differential Neural Network for Solving Nonlinear and Nonconvex Optimization Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Nonlinear nonconvex optimization problem (NNOP) holds significant importance across various scientific fields as a common problem in engineering applications. To achieve fast convergence and strong robustness within a limited time when solving NNOPs, a novel penalty strategy finite-time convergent-differential neural network (PS-FT-CDNN) is presented. The equality constraints in NNOPs are transformed into penalty terms in the objective function through penalty functions. Then, Based on the design method of convergent differential neural networks, PS-FT-CDNN is designed to solve NNOPs with multiple constraints. The results of computer simulations confirm that the proposed PS-FT-CDNN achieves faster error convergence and demonstrates superior robustness compared to existing neural networks when addressing NNOPs with equality and inequality constraints.

articleTitle: Discrete Time-Varying Equality Constrained Optimization: A Zeroing Neural Dynamic Method with Two Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In this paper, the discrete time-varying equality constrained optimization (D-TV-ECO) problem based on discrete-time zeroing neural dynamic (DT-ZND) method is studied. Firstly, a continuous time-varying equality constrained optimization (C-TV-ECO) problem is presented. Secondly, the Lagrange function is constructed by introducing the Lagrange method, which integrates the objective function and related constraints into a continuous time-varying system. Then, a continuous-time ZND (CT-ZND) method is built. Afterward, using the discretization derivation method based on the expansion of four-step ZeaD formula (FsZF), a FsZF DT-ZND method for D-TV-ECO problem is proposed, which has two design parameters, including discretization parameter and convergence parameter. Significantly, the truncation error of the FsZF DT-ZND method has been elevated to the fourth-order, thereby enhancing the precision of the calculations. Theoretical analysis indicates that the FsZF DT-ZND method exhibits convergence and stability. In the numerical experiments, the impact of different values of the discretization parameter α and convergence parameter κ is analyzed. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to further demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the FsZF DT-ZND method.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy-Power Direct-Discretization RNN Algorithm for Solving Discrete Multilayer Dynamic Systems With Robotic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This work proposes a new recurrent neural network (RNN) algorithm for solving discrete multilayer dynamic systems (DMDSs). First, by utilizing the direct-discretization technique, a direct-discretization RNN (DDRNN) algorithm for solving the DMDSs is introduced. On this basis, a fuzzy-power direct-discretization RNN (FDDRNN) algorithm is proposed, which integrates a fuzzy control system (FCS) within the DDRNN framework. This integration dynamically modulates the time step τ by exerting a fuzzy-power factor r, which is determined based on the logarithm of the residual, as τ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup>. Finally, comparative evaluations among the gradient-based RNN (GBRNN), the DDRNN, and the FDDRNN algorithms are conducted through numerical experiments and robotic application experiments involving both planar and spatial robots. The results indicate that the proposed FDDRNN algorithm outperforms the GBRNN and DDRNN algorithms in terms of accuracy, convergence speed, and stability.

articleTitle: Causal Actions Recognition for Efficient Exploration in Robotic Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: When using deep reinforcement learning to handle a robot task, it is necessary to learn a policy that outputs the actions the robot should execute. This policy needs to be learned through the robot’s continuous trial-and-error interactions with the environment. The robot may have the capability to perform multiple actions, but in fact, it doesn’t need to use all of these actions to complete the current task. It can reduce unnecessary exploration during reinforcement learning by using only those actions that impact task completion. This paper introduces a causality-based approach to identify essential robotic actions for task completion, utilizing environmental interactions for more accurate causal action identification than manual selection. And an experimental comparison on a multi-stage task demonstrates that constructing the action space using only the robot’s causal actions can facilitate more effective learning.

articleTitle: Improved A* Algorithm and Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance Method for Path Planning and Self- Positioning of Autonomous Guided Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: As Autonomous Guided Vehicles (AGV) are becoming more and more widely used, they demand safe and reliable autonomous navigation solutions to problems including how to plan a safe and efficient path based on known environmental information, how to accurately self-locate, and how to precisely avoid obstacles during the navigation process. These problems have given rise to path planning algorithms that have been the focus of research in the field of intelligent robot control. This paper develops new methods for path planning and self-positioning. Firstly, it develops the improved A* algorithm by constructing a heuristic function and increasing the weight of the heuristic cost. The improved algorithm significantly reduces the computation of the traversal of irrelevant node points and hence the computation time. Further it adds a smoothing process for unsmooth paths using Bessel curves, resulting in sufficiently smooth curve. Simulations of the algorithm show that the improved A* algorithm can significantly reduce the number of nodes traversed while ensuring optimal paths. Secondly, in terms of self-positioning, the distance between the visual tag and the robot is analyzed using the visual tag information acquired by the robot vision system to determine the position and orientation of the robot. To achieve collision avoidance during navigation in dynamic environments, a dynamic obstacle avoidance method is proposed, which combines TOF sensors to acquire local environment information; dynamic obstacle avoidance is achieved by inserting and switching tracking sub-targets. Finally, path planning tests were carried out using the AGV. Results show that the method can meet the needs of AGV applications in complex and dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of intelligent wearable system for lower limb rehabilitation robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of poor comfort, narrow application range and complicated wearing of the existing lower limb rehabilitation equipment, an intelligent wearable device is designed in this paper. With reference to the size range of human lower limbs, smart wearables for different patients are designed and verified by experiments. Combined with 3D printing technology and airbag technology, the parts required for the experiment are made, the force situation is collected by the thin film pressure sensor, and the program is written and burned by Arduino. The results show that the device not only enhances the fit degree and comfort by using the compressibility of the air bag, but also increases the contact area between the exoskeleton and the lower limb, reduces the error caused by relative sliding, improves the personalized adaptation ability, and provides a new reference for the development of exoskeleton technology in the future.

articleTitle: Hybrid Obstacle Avoidance and Repetitive Motion Scheme of Mobile Robots Synthesized by Varying-Parameter Dynamic Learning Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In order to effectively avoid obstacles and resolve non-repetitive problems of mobile redundant manipulators, a hybrid obstacle avoidance and repetitive motion (HOARM) scheme is proposed, analyzed, and applied, which is synthesized by varying-parameter dynamic learning networks (VPDLN). Specifically, to guarantee the efficient and accurate tasks, a periodic relaxation constrained repetitive motion scheme and an obstacle avoidance approach are integrated as a quadratic criterion, then a bicriteria scheme is constructed by combining the schemes and kinematic models of mobile redundant manipulators, and is further deduced as a quadratic programming (QP) problem through a dynamic weighting method. Then a varying-parameter dynamic learning networks method is applied to solve the proposed QP problem. Furthermore, a path-tracking task is conducted to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed HOARM scheme.

articleTitle: Time-optimal trajectory planning of a six-degree-of-freedom robotic arm based on improved PSO algorithm
