publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: To increase the working efficiency of the robotic arm and its stability, a 3-5-3 polynomial interpolation trajectory optimization algorithm based on the improved particle swarm algorithm is proposed for the time-optimal planning problem of a 6-DOF robotic arm. The improved particle swarm optimization algorithm improves the algorithm's global search ability and local search ability by nonlinearly and dynamically adjusting the size of inertia weights and learning factors. The improved particle swarm algorithm is used to optimize the robotic arm motion trajectory in the shortest time under the constraints such as speed. The research results show that the optimized particle swarm algorithm has higher optimization accuracy and faster convergence speed, and the overall running time of the robotic arm optimized by the improved algorithm is shorter, which verifies the effectiveness of the algorithm. And through the matlab software for robotic arm simulation experiments, to verify the reliability of the time-optimized robotic arm trajectory.

articleTitle: Tilt-Rotor Vertical Takeoff and Landing UAV Oblique Takeoff Trajectory Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In this paper, for the tilt-rotor vertical takeoff and landing vehicle takeoff multi-constraint trajectory optimization problem, the optimal takeoff trajectory optimization design based on the Gauss pseudo-spectral method is carried out, and the optimal takeoff trajectory of energy consumption and time is derived. The optimal control problem model of the tilted takeoff optimal trajectory optimization problem is established, discretized by Gauss pseudo-spectral method, and transformed into a nonlinear planning problem for solving. The mathematical simulation results show that the optimization result meets the constraints, reaches the target landing point with zero speed, and meets the optimization objective of optimal fuel consumption.

articleTitle: Research on accuracy range of shaft-hole assembly with robot based on image recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In this paper, the automatic assembly of shaft-hole with robot is researched, and the accuracy range of robot shaft -hole assembly based on image recognition algorithm is explored. According to the accuracy experiment requirements, the robot system and shaft-hole assembly platform are built, the eye-in-hand system calibration scheme is designed. A recognition algorithm combining image preprocessing technology, edge detection and Hough transform circle detection is proposed to locate the mounting hole and realize the shaft-hole assembly with the robot. In order to improve the image recognition process, image preprocessing technologies such as gray level processing, Gaussian filter are used to reduce the influence of the surrounding environment and noise points. Edge detection with Sobel operator is adopted to enhance the target features of the image and improve the accuracy of circle center recognition. Hole center coordinates is obtained by Hough transform circle detection. Finally, the hand-eye relationship obtained by calibration is used to drive the robot to realize the shaft-hole assembly. In order to obtain the accuracy range of shaft-hole assembly, several experiments were carried out, and the experimental results showed that the error of shaft-hole assembly is limited to ±1 mm.

articleTitle: LDUNet: a Lung Dense U-Net to segment the lung parenchyma from CT images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Automatic segmentation of lung parenchyma from computed tomography (CT) images can assist doctors in diagnosing lung cancer. The traditional lung parenchyma segmentation algorithm has poor generalization ability, and the segmentation result of CT image including pulmonary trachea and pulmonary vessels is not ideal. Hence, a LDUNet based on deep convolutional neural network is proposed in this paper for automatically segment the lung parenchyma. In order to reduce the problems of over fitting and gradient disappearance, a novel Dense block is proposed for the Encoder part of LDUNet, and the effectiveness of the Dense block is proved by ablation experiments. Secondly, SE channel attention mechanism is introduced to skip connection to reuse the high-resolution information lost in the encoding process efficiently, so that the target image generated in the decoding process is more accurate. The paper has carried out a lot of experiments based on the public LIDC-IDRI dataset, and finally achieved 99.48% accuracy rate in lung parenchymal segmentation, which is superior to most advanced segmentation models. Experimental results show that LDUNet has good accuracy and robustness in lung parenchyma segmentation.

articleTitle: Home garden robot based on Internet of Things technology, plant 3D data features and spherical calibration and registration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: As living standards and material culture improve, the demands for private home garden landscaping have also increased. People no longer limit their expectations for home garden landscapes to the combination of plants and greening functions; instead, there is a greater emphasis on personalization, innovation, and aesthetics. To lower the design threshold for individuals in the home garden landscape design process and enhance the integrated management of plant disease diagnosis, growth analysis, pruning, and cultivation, this paper presents a home garden robot based on Internet of Things (IoT) technology, neural radiance fields (NeRF) for three-dimensional data feature extraction, and spherical calibration registration. This innovation significantly improves the beautification efficiency and quality of home gardens.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Penetration Technology of High Speed Flight Vehicle Based on PPO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In this paper, a high speed flight vehicle intelligent control method based on the proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm is researched. This method can be used to avoid the impact of interceptor employing the pure proportional navigation (PPN) guidance strategy in three dimensions. First, the interception process of the interceptor and the penetration process of the flight vehicle in the actual scenario were analyzed. The flight vehicle kinematic model, the interceptor kinematic model based on the PPN guidance law, and the relative motion model were constructed. Then, a flight vehicle intelligent penetration guidance law training model was built with specific scenarios. PPO-based model structure, state space, action space, reward function and training end conditions were designed. Finally, an intelligent flight vehicle penetration control model is formed through training, and the effectiveness of the proposed penetration method is verified through simulation tests. The method is applied to penetrate other performance interceptors and compared with other maneuvering strategies. The results verify the robustness and significant advantages of the intelligent penetration method. The intelligent penetration method studied in this paper has certain reference value for the flight vehicle guidance law design.

articleTitle: An OCBA-Based Information Sharing Method for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Recent technological advancements in renewable energy generation, fuel cells, and energy storage systems have intensified research interest in supply-demand matching within smart grids. This challenge often involves hundreds of thousands of agents making real-time decisions. In the context of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), critical questions arise regarding what information should be shared among agents and how to effectively utilize this shared data. These questions remain largely unresolved, primarily due to the inherent complexity and the variability of the subproblems faced by each agent. We consider this important problem in this work, and make the following major contributions. First, we formulate a framework aimed at maximizing the probability of selecting the optimal action in a given state while operating under a limited sampling budget. Second, we propose an algorithm designed to asymptotically maximize the probability of correct selection (PCS) when all agents are dealing with the same Markov decision process (MDP). Finally, we perform our method on a supply demand matching problem and show its efficiency. We hope this work can bring insights to efficient sampling in MARL in more general situations.

articleTitle: Multi-robot local path planning based on an improved dynamic window algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) algorithm, referred to as WE-DWA, designed to address the shortcomings of traditional DWA in terms of safety, flexibility, and advanced planning capabilities in complex environments. By incorporating path loop detection and reverse motion mechanisms, the new algorithm avoids repetitive paths; adaptive adjustments to speed and angular velocity enhance the algorithm's flexibility; and a path coordination mechanism is employed to consider the collaboration among robots. These enhancements significantly improve the obstacle avoidance and path planning capabilities of the DWA algorithm in complex environments, providing an efficient and flexible solution for multi-robot systems. Simulation experiments have validated the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Multi-Layer Alignment and Adaptive Weighting Framework for Multi-Task Model Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The integration of multi-task learning models presents challenges, particularly in addressing task-specific interference and enhancing cross-task knowledge transfer. To tackle these issues, we propose the Multi-Layer Task Alignment Weighted Fusion Model (MTAWM), a novel approach that optimizes model fusion by aligning tasks hierarchically and applying an adaptive weighting mechanism. MTAWM synchronizes task-specific layers using a Linear Mode Connectivity (LMC) strategy to prevent inter-layer parameter conflicts, while an adaptive weighting mechanism prioritizes task influence according to significance. Additionally, cross-layer consistency regularization is introduced to minimize deviations and stabilize the fusion process. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that MTAWM achieves superior performance in task accuracy, consistency, and model robustness when compared to existing baseline methods, positioning it as a robust solution for multi-task learning environments. MTAWM’s framework not only advances task alignment in multi-task settings but also holds potential for broader applications in multimodal data processing.

articleTitle: Integration of Emotional-Cognitive Architecture in ACT-R for Multi-Agent Social Dynamics for Disaster Response Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Accurately simulating human behavior in disaster scenarios is crucial for effective emergency management and social response prediction. However, existing approaches lack integration of emotional factors in cognitive modeling, leading to limited fidelity in behavioral simulation. This study presents an enhanced ACT-R framework incorporating an emotional module to simulate post-disaster social dynamics, with a specific focus on earthquake scenarios. We propose a novel integration methodology that combines ACT-R with Agent-Based Modeling (ABM), where emotional states are dynamically modeled through a triple-parameter system (emotional intensity, social support level, and resource availability) that adaptively influences cognitive processing and decision thresholds. By implementing this emotion-aware framework in a case study of 20,000 agents within Xi'an city wall area, we observed distinct emotional clustering patterns and collective safety-seeking behaviors driven by emotional contagion, demonstrating the framework's capability in capturing complex social dynamics during crisis scenarios.

articleTitle: Vehicle Adaptive Cruise Control Based on Model Predictive Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: With the development of the information age and electric vehicles, there is an increasing demand for highly safe and comfortable driving experiences. Autonomous driving, based on adaptive cruise systems, has emerged in response to these needs. As one of the most critical technologies in vehicle ADAS, adaptive cruise systems have always been a focal point in the research of autonomous driving technology. These systems can control vehicle speed, distance, and lane-changing operations through various sensors and decision-making facilities during long-distance driving, thereby reducing driver fatigue and enhancing driving comfort. At the same time, adaptive cruise systems carry out safer operations by precisely perceiving the environment and performing accurate calculations, meeting the demand for a safe and comfortable driving environment. The paper predicts vehicle behavior using the MPC (Model Predictive Control) algorithm based on the principles of adaptive cruise systems. The intelligent decision-making and optimization instructions of the adaptive cruise system module are then used to control the vehicle’s power, braking, and other systems to execute the commands. A simulation platform was built using Matlab/Simulink software to simulate working conditions such as distance control. The experimental results show that the MPC algorithm enhances the precision of the vehicle’s following movement in the cruise system, demonstrating better practical effects. It adapts to various traffic environments and ensures greater stability and safety during driving.

articleTitle: Detection of pulmonary nodule lesions based on improved Mask R-CNN algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Lung cancer primarily develops from malignant nodules in the lungs. Early screening of lung nodules is crucial for detecting early-stage lung cancer. However, early lung nodules often lack distinct features, and the presence of non-pulmonary parenchymal areas and lung soft tissues significantly interferes with their differentiation and detection. To address the characteristics of pulmonary CT images, an improved Mask R-CNN lung nodule detection model is proposed, incorporating deep learning techniques. A hybrid attention mechanism is introduced into the feature backbone network to establish spatial and channel relationships within the feature maps, thereby enhancing the model's ability to extract features from the target and improving the correlation of shallow feature information. Additionally, the anchor box sizes are modified to five new dimensions to better capture the features of lung nodules of varying sizes during the detection process. Experimental validation of the improved algorithm demonstrates a detection sensitivity of 89.7%, an average segmentation similarity coefficient of 96%, and an average precision of 88.1%.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Localization Method for Underground Space Targets Based on the Fusion of Camera and LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The search and positioning of underground space targets are of significant importance in various fields. However, existing technologies still exhibit low efficiency and accuracy in complex underground scenarios. This paper proposes an intelligent positioning method for underground space targets based on the fusion of cameras and LiDAR. Firstly, the real-time detection of underground targets via a camera is performed, then it combines LiDAR point cloud maps to calculate the position of each element in the current image within the reference frame of the constructed point cloud map. Finally, a fusion and deduplication strategy is employed to suppress duplicate targets. The resulting target positioning distribution map provides an effective and intuitive representation of the reconnaissance results for underground targets.

articleTitle: Pest Rat Detection and Capture System in Barn
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: With the development of agricultural automation and intelligence, pest rat monitoring in barns becomes more and more important. The traditional rat detection method has problems such as low precision and poor efficiency, which is difficult to meet the practical needs. In this paper, an improved method for rat detection in barn is proposed based on YOLOv5 algorithm. First, in order to improve the detection accuracy, a multi-scale feature fusion strategy is adopted, which improves the network structure in order to better capture the features of rats at different scales; second, data enhancement techniques, including image rotation, scaling, and color transformations, are used to enhance the robustness and generalization ability of the model. Finally, in order to improve the real-time detection capability, lightweight network design and quantization techniques are used to reduce the computational and parameter numbers of the model, thus achieving faster detection. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv5 model has a greater improvement in both accuracy and detection speed compared to the original YOLOv5 model on the rat detection task. The method proposed in this paper has greater potential for application in agricultural surveillance and provides technical support for automated pest rat control.

articleTitle: A method of replacing failed GIS equipment in a restricted space
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: When a substation was carrying out the local discharge test of 220kV busbar switch, it was found that there was a suspected local discharge signal in the switching interval of 220kV #1M-#2M busbar 2012. After detailed investigation of the signal, it was confirmed that the discharge signal originated from within the GIS and was not caused by interference from the external environment. Further through comparative analysis and based on the propagation characteristics of the discharge signal, we deduced that the approximate location of the discharge source is located in the area from the 2012 interval to the 2M busbar. In view of the above, the knife gate equipment at this location needs to be replaced. The purpose of this paper is to explain in detail, in such a space-limited area, how to skillfully build a support platform and set up a rail panning system, to minimize the scope of power outages and reduce the scope of equipment removal under the premise of the equipment to complete the replacement of efficient and safe operations.

articleTitle: Designing of a Dexterous Hand and Performance Evaluation Based on Teleoperation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: We proposed to design and evaluate a dexterous robotic hand through teleoperation. We introduced a dexterous hand with four fully actuated fingers, providing 16 degrees of freedom. A motor independently controls each joint, ensuring precise and flexible movements. The design incorporates an innovative joint distribution structure, enhancing the hand’s flexibility and grasping capabilities. To validate the effectiveness of the design, we conducted a series of real-world experiments where the robotic hand replicated natural finger movements based on human hand gestures. The results demonstrated that the hand pose retargeting method successfully translates human gestures into precise and functional robotic hand movements, highlighting its potential for various practical applications in robotics.

articleTitle: A Pump Fault Warning Algorithm Based on Improved PCA-KNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In the industrial field, Water pumps are key equipment for fluid transportation in the industrial field, and the fault warning of water pumps is of great significance for ensuring the continuity and safety of production. This article proposes a pump fault warning method based on improved principal component analysis (PCA) and K-nearest neighbor (KNN) algorithm. Firstly, by improving PCA for dimensionality reduction of water pump operation data, the main features are effectively extracted to reduce data redundancy. Subsequently, the KNN algorithm was used to classify the reduced dimensional data for identifying fault states. The experimental results show that this method has significant advantages in both accuracy and response speed of fault detection, and can warn potential faults timely, reduce downtime and maintenance costs. The method presented in this article provides an effective approach for water pump fault warning and has promising application prospects.

articleTitle: Time-Varying ZAI (Zhang Approximation Inverse) and SE (Simple "Optimal") Alternative Proposed for Solving Nonlinear Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Approximation inverse and nonlinear equations are critical topics in contemporary research. In this paper, we propose and utilize the concept of time-varying Zhang approximation inverse (TV-ZAI) to approximate the inverse of time-varying Jacobian matrix, and to solve the nonlinear equation. Specifically, we propose the norm based definitions and spectral-radius (SR) based definitions to complement the TV-ZAI. The TV-ZAI is capable of dealing with both continuous and discrete time-varying problems, which makes it more efficient in computation and easier to implement in digital computers compared with analog computers. In addition, we propose a simple alternative for the time-varying optimal Zhang approximation inverse (TV-OZAI). Besides, the corresponding numerical experimental results show the feasibility and effectiveness of the TV-ZAI and TV-OZAI-alternative solutions for solving nonlinear equations.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV continuous power inspection scheduling algorithm based on NSGA-III
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper focuses on addressing the optimization scheduling problem of multi-UAV power inspection tasks. In the context of power inspections, it is often not feasible for a single UAV to complete the inspection due to limitations such as power endurance, UAV hardware constraints, and task settings. Consequently, multiple UAVs are required to perform inspections in a continuous manner. The study models the complex scenario of power line inspection as a multi-objective optimization problem, considering various risk factors associated with UAV operations. By examining these risks, the study proposes a solution based on the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) algorithm. The proposed approach aims to minimize both the total risk and the maximum risk faced by UAVs during the inspection process. Comparative experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The results demonstrate that, compared to traditional rule-based methods, the NSGA-III algorithm significantly reduces both total risk and maximum risk, ensuring efficient and safe power inspection. Furthermore, the study also considers the failure continuation case, where the remaining UAVs can effectively take over and complete the inspection tasks in case of failure of one UAV. This contributes to the development of more reliable and robust UAV-based power inspection techniques.

articleTitle: Microexpression Classification Based on Vision Transformer and Fusion Super-Resolution Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: With the advancement of artificial intelligence technology, microexpression recognition has garnered significant attention in the fields of public services and lie detection. It is an essential tool for understanding human emotions and non-verbal communication. However, due to the brevity and subtlety of microexpressions, research in this area faces numerous challenges, including limited image datasets, low image resolution, diverse categories, and insufficient model generalization capabilities. To address these issues, a microexpression image classification method based on Vision Transformer (ViT) and fusion super-resolution technology is proposed. This method leverages the strengths of super-resolution technology and the ViT model. The fusion dataset method, which utilizes a diffusion model for super-resolution, can effectively expand the microexpression dataset. Furthermore, the ViT model can effectively enhance the feature extraction ability for microexpression images. After applying this method to extract image features, the validation accuracy of the experimental dataset increased from 66.99% to 92.59%, representing a 25.6% improvement. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method of integrating ViT with fusion super-resolution effectively enhances the accuracy of microexpression image classification, providing a valuable reference for the application and development of microexpression recognition and classification technology in areas such as teaching activities, psychological research, and the legal field.

articleTitle: Improved Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control With a Novel Extended State Disturbance Observer for PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: For the sake of solving the undesirable chattering in the conventional super-twisting sliding mode controller (STSMC), this paper proposes an improved STSMC and a novel extended state observer (ESO) for the drives of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). First, an elliptic saturation function is designed to construct the improved STSMC and its finite-time convergence is analyzed. Therefore, a novel ESO is introduced to diminish the switching gain and compensate the lumped disturbance of the PMSM system. Ultimately, the results of simulation demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces chattering while enhancing dynamic response and robustness.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of ML Algorithms and FPGA Accelerators for Robotic Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Integrating machine learning (ML) algorithms into robotic intelligence necessitates balancing accuracy, resource efficiency, and energy consumption. This study presents the Multi-Objective Optimization Co-Design (MOO-CoD) framework, developed to enhance both ML algorithms and their corresponding hardware accelerators for robotic applications. MOO-CoD simultaneously optimizes algorithms and hardware through MOO techniques, including weighted optimization, accuracy-prioritized approaches, and Pareto front analysis, to achieve optimal model performance and resource efficiency. By leveraging FPGA accelerators, the MOO-CoD framework enables rapid ML deployment with scalable, high-performance hardware designs, making it ideal for low-latency and energy-efficient robotic systems. Empirical evaluations using the NGSIM and SECOM datasets demonstrate that MOO-CoD significantly reduces resource consumption while maintaining high AUC scores. These results highlight the framework’s effectiveness in addressing critical challenges in robotic intelligence by enhancing both ML performance and hardware efficiency.

articleTitle: AUD:AU-based Diffusion model for Facial Expression Synthesis from a Single Image
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Facial expression editing technology can significantly enhance the human-computer interaction experience. Recent developments in Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have yielded remarkable outcomes in the realm of facial expression synthesis, by shaping the generation process with images featuring different emotions. Although successful, GAN-based methods are limited to producing a finite number of expressions based on the dataset’s contents. To overcome this constraint, this study introduces the AUD: AU-based Diffusion model for Facial Expression Synthesis. This novel approach comprises two main stages: modulation and editing. The modulation phase entails training through the re-targeting of a pre-existing diffusion-based language-image model for expression refinement. We employed an AU-aware fine-tuning strategy to enhance the distinction between AUs related to facial expressions and irrelevant characteristics. In the editing stage, an initial inversion technique is applied to convert the input image into latent noise. Subsequently, a set of text cues encompassing both the initial and target AU vectors are utilized for text-guided localized emotion enhancement, facilitated by attention control. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations indicate that our methodology, which is the first work to integrate diffusion models with expression editing, excels in generating high-quality images with subtle, continuous expressions, and emotion accuracy score(EmoACC) for specific generated emotions surpass the SOTA performance.

articleTitle: A Review of Deep Learning-Enhanced Imaging Methods for Microrobots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Microrobots have emerged as effective tools for non-invasive tasks related to biomedical applications, such as drug delivery. Their operation in complex environments, such as in vivo applications, requires accurate real-time imaging techniques. However, imaging methods usually present several challenges, such as low contrast, limited spatiotemporal resolution, and restricted depth penetration. To address these issues, deep learning (DL) offers an effective solution by automatic extraction of features from microrobot images, even with dense backgrounds. This paper reviews recent advancements to enhance biomedical imaging methods, such as optical, magnetic field-based, and ultrasound-based methods, by using DL algorithms for the detection and tracking of microrobots. It also highlights the existing challenges and offers directions for future studies in improving imaging performance and extending the scope of the application of microrobots.

articleTitle: Garbage Image Classification Using Improved Inception-V3 Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper presents an improved Inception-V3 model for garbage image classification aimed at facilitating intelligent garbage sorting through computer vision or mobile terminal applications. Initially, the iPhone-GARBAGE dataset of garbage images is constructed. Subsequently, the convolution blocks in the original Inception-V3 are replaced with new Inverted Bottleneck modules for richer feature expressions. Additionally, a Contextual Transformer module is added, enabling the model to discern more detailed object and scene semantics. The substitution of multi-scale pooling layers for the conventional maximum pooling layers further enhances the model's capability to recognize and retain features. Lastly, the integration of data augmentation and transfer learning strategies into the deep convolutional network empowers the recognition and classification of garbage images. Comparative experiments with different models under identical conditions are conducted. Results indicate that the improved Inception-V3 model achieves a classification accuracy of 96.20% and a test accuracy of 96.10%, surpassing other models. The proposed model demonstrates faster improvement rates and better convergence.

articleTitle: Enhanced Robotic Arm Localization Using UKF Based on Joint Angles and Camera Observations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: While vision-based methods for self-localization are well-established in mobile robotics, the use of machine vision for end-effector positioning in robotic arms remains comparatively less explored. This work presents a simulation framework for efficient multi-robotic arm collaboration, enabling precise end-effector monitoring across multiple arms. Traditional spline-based trajectory planning is employed to ensure smoother and more efficient control. The framework integrates a YOLO model for fast target recognition and an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) to enhance robustness against noise impact, ensuring reliable performance in networked environments. Developed in Webots with UR5e robotic arms, this framework demonstrates high portability across platforms with minimal code modification and achieves millimeter-level accuracy, providing a cost-effective solution for multi-robot perception and collaborative robotic arm research.

articleTitle: A baseline determination of flywheel maneuver performance based on Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: As a prerequisite for satellite component health assessment, the performance baseline has important reference significance and engineering value for ensuring safe and reliable satellite operation and mission success, and at the same time, it can provide scientific basis and theoretical and methodological support for the reasonable classification and determination of component health states. This paper takes the flywheel in attitude maneuvering mode as the research object, and constructs a multi-domain performance feature indicator set by analyzing the working mechanism of the flywheel in the maneuvering mode and selecting suitable health feature parameters. Secondly, a performance baseline establishment method based on the Transformer neural network model is proposed, and the hidden mapping relationship between the health feature parameters and the dynamic performance indicators is explored by using multi-head attention mechanism. Finally, the validity of the baseline model of the flywheel in maneuvering mode mentioned in this paper is verified by building a simulation platform.

articleTitle: CMCY: A Dual Closed-loop Social Physics Cognitive Model for Youth Education via Virtual-Real Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Despite advances in computational modeling and virtual-real interactive technologies, current youth cognitive development systems face significant challenges in real-time assessment accuracy, adaptive feedback mechanisms, and integrated measurement of cognitive-behavioral-emotional dimensions. We propose CMCY (Cognitive Model for Contemporary Youth), a novel social physics-based framework that implements dual closed-loop feedback mechanisms for adaptive cognitive assessment and enhancement. The methodological framework employs the CDIO (Conceive-Design-Implement-Operate) educational paradigm to systematically evaluate cognitive development across three dimensions: cognitive processing (memory, understanding, application), behavioral execution (imitation, coordination, creation), and emotional response (interest, reflection, character formation). The system implements computational experimental methods through prediction-experimentation-iteration cycles, utilizing both virtual product patterns and physical interaction data. This research contributes to the fundamental understanding of youth cognitive development mechanisms while providing a scalable technological framework for practical educational applications.

articleTitle: An accurate prediction method of robot machining deformation error under force-position data fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Robots, with their high flexibility and extensive working space, have emerged as a new manufacturing paradigm following traditional machine tool production. However, due to factors such as the weak joint rigidity of their serial structures, time-varying dynamic processing loads, and workspace heterogeneity, significant workpiece deformation errors occur during machining. Force-position data directly reflect the physical interactions of the machining process and contain deeper feature information. To address this, a prediction model of robotic machining deformation error based on Autoencoder-Temporal Convolutional Network (AE-TCN) force-position data fusion is proposed. The model leverages AE to achieve multidimensional feature fusion of raw data and TCN with causal dilated convolutions to enable efficient parallel computation while capturing the temporal dependencies in the robotic machining process. The model demonstrated exceptional performance in linear milling tasks on flat plates. Four generalization tasks were designed to validate its effectiveness and strong generalization capabilities: parameter differentiation, trajectory differentiation, workpiece profile differentiation, and workpiece profile-parameter differentiation. Comparative analyses confirmed the proposed method's robustness and adaptability. Additionally, owing to the post-measurement nature of workpiece deformation errors and the lightweight design of the model, it outperforms other complex models by enabling efficient inference for online tasks, making it highly significant for real-time applications.

articleTitle: An Embodied Collaborative Search Strategy for Multi-Scale Visual Feature Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Compared to canines, quadruped robots offer significant advantages, including lower training costs, ease of large-scale deployment, and reduced maintenance burdens. As quadruped robot technology has gradually matured, most studies have focused on the kinematics and navigation of quadruped robots with limited research on collaborative search tasks involving canines and biomimetic robots. To develop a quadruped robot guidance system that enhances search success rates, this study addresses the demand for collaborative operations between canines and quadruped robots. This study proposes a multi-scale visual target perception mechanism, which is based on confidence region estimation. This mechanism strengthens adaptability to target scale variations in complex scenes, enabling more accurate target recognition. Inspired by traditional tracking dog training methods, we propose an embodied collaborative and efficient search strategy. We evaluate the strategy by testing the success rates of target search tasks in both daytime and nighttime indoor environments. The embodied collaborative search strategy improves, recognition speed by approximately 62.5% in dark environments and 35.3% in illuminated environments, compared to traditional single canine search tasks and the overall task completion rate is also improved. This was shown in a number of different experimental scenarios that took place in different spatiotemporal settings.

articleTitle: A Novel Power Equipment Heating Trend Prediction Model Based on Improved Informer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Power equipment is an important part of the power system, and its impending failures are often accompanied by abnormal heating. Therefore, predicting and tracking the future heating trends of power equipment is important for the stable operation of the power system. In this paper, an improved Informer model, Informer-KDC, is proposed for heating trend prediction of power equipment. In Informer-KDC, first, dilated causal convolution is used to increase the receptive field of the model. Secondly, a new residual connection is introduced to preserve more original feature information and weaken the possibility of network degradation. Finally, the Kernel-MSE loss function is utilized to address the nonlinearity of errors, enhancing the model's predictive performance. The proposed Informer-KDC model improves upon the Informer model in both network architecture and loss function, significantly increasing prediction accuracy. Experiments conducted on the widely used ETT long-term time series dataset and the ECL power load dataset demonstrate that the Informer-KDC model exhibits outstanding predictive performance, achieving the best performance metrics on both datasets.

articleTitle: Vision Language Model Empowered Surgical Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The integration of a flexible endoscope with a surgical manipulator is crucial in minimally invasive surgery (MIS), facilitating detailed visualization of the operative field within the patient’s body. During MIS, the remote center of motion (RCM) constraints are essential for achieving visual servoing control and ensuring accurate tracking control of the robotic endoscope. Existing work requires the exact trajectory for the tracking control and does not connect both tasks with the RCM constraints. In this paper, we exploit GPT-V to develop Vision Language Model Empowered surgical Planning (VLM-EP), which uses environmental observations and task description to finish the tracking task without the exact trajectory and connect both tasks through the exploration procedure in vivo safety range. Our simulated experiments show that our VLM-EP significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art control-based baseline. We demonstrate a practical implementation of VLM-EP in real-world scenarios, which shows that VLM-EP effectively handles the tracking control task and the visual servoing control task.

articleTitle: A Method for Ranking the Importance of Command and Communication Network Nodes Based on Complex Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In order to address the issue of node importance ranking in command and communication network, the basic principles of complex networks were adopted to propose two basic models: unweighted undirected networks and weighted undirected networks. Three typical structures, namely tree, grid, and hybrid structures, were established, and the importance of nodes is comprehensively quantified using four indicators: degree centrality, betweenness centrality, connectivity, and network efficiency. The experiment shows that the ranking method proposed in the paper can accurately and efficiently identify important nodes, providing a reference for the application and guarantee of command and communication network.

Index Terms: Importance Of Nodes In The Network

articleTitle: A Pull Drift Compensation Strategy for Heavy Commercial Vehicles with Electric Power Steering Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: Vehicle driving wandering is a common failure mode that affects the performance of vehicles. Due to the greater mass and higher center of gravity of commercial vehicles compared to passenger cars, pull drift not only increases driver fatigue but also increases the risk of rollover. Therefore, designing an effective compensation plan for commercial vehicle pull drift is an important and challenging issue. In this paper, based on the pull drift mechanism of heavy commercial vehicles, we propose an electric power steering pull drift compensation strategy for heavy commercial vehicles. Through three stages of functional scene recognition, compensation torque calculation, and compensation torque output, it can directly generate the torque demand for the steering system motor. Simulation experiments show that this method can accurately and quickly recognize pull drift scenarios and effectively reduce vehicle lateral error and roll angle.

articleTitle: Improved RRT-D*: Algorithm Fusion for Optimal Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: The rapidly exploring random tree (RRT) is a widely used algorithm in path planning. However, the algorithm has an excessively large sampling range, overly random sampling, and numerous invalid iterations. Additionally, the algorithm path is not optimal; it cannot avoid obstacles dynamically, and the generated route is not sufficiently smooth, which limits its use. To overcome these problems, we propose the improved RRT* algorithm that enhances the RRT algorithm in terms of two aspects: target sampling in adaptive environments and adaptive dynamic step size strategy. It then integrates the improved RRT and D* algorithms to enhance the quality and efficiency of track generation. After obtaining a feasible path planned using the improved RRT algorithm, the feasible area was expanded to the surrounding area and rasterized. The D* algorithm was used to determine the shortest path in the feasible area, and the fused algorithm was suitable for dynamic obstacle avoidance. Finally, the path length, number of path inflection points, and path planning time were used as evaluation indicators to compare the improved RRT-D* algorithm with the RRT and improved RRT algorithms. The simulation results show that the improved RRTD* algorithm is more efficient and dynamically avoids obstacles. This study provides a new approach to improving sampling algorithms and application effectiveness.

articleTitle: General event detection algorithm of audio and video based on multimodal models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the general event detection task of audio and video from the perspective of pre-trained feature extractor. To solve the problem that the existing work lacks the ability to effectively use multi-modal large model feature modeling in this downstream task, this paper proposes an audio and video general event detection algorithm based on AudioCLIP adapter and time-domain multi-scale fusion network based on cross-modal attention. The method consists of two training stages: 1) In the first stage, a linear adapter is used to adjust the features of the pre-trained model to adapt to the downstream task; 2) In the second stage, the multi-scale fusion network is proposed to strengthen the model's context-dependent modeling ability of events by using timing information of different scales. This method can effectively adapt to pre-trained large models and enhance the time series information fusion of audio and video features. The experimental results show that on the AVE dataset, the proposed method achieves 79.36% overall classification accuracy, which is 6.66% higher than that of the baseline method, and has strong event detection capability.

articleTitle: Research on Task Allocation for Continuous Transmission Line Inspection Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper systematically explores the task allocation challenge within the realm of power inspection, particularly addressing the issue that power inspections often cannot be completed by a single drone due to limitations in power endurance, UAV hardware, and task configurations. Consequently, multiple drones must perform the inspection in a continuous manner. Leveraging the sophisticated framework of reinforcement learning, the study commences by delineating a comprehensive modeling methodology, meticulously elucidating the pivotal components of task allocation, namely the state space, action space, and the reward function design. These foundational elements establish the theoretical underpinnings for the subsequent deployment of reinforcement learning algorithms. Subsequently, the Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithm is adopted, wherein we initially train individual task allocation models tailored for single and dual unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) scenarios. Subsequent to this, these models are integrated to construct a hybrid reinforcement learning framework. The empirical findings reveal that both the single UAV task allocation model and the dual UAV task allocation model exhibit distinct limitations: the former demonstrating shortcomings in safety, while the latter lacks efficiency. When comparing the composite reinforcement learning model with the traditional reinforcement learning model, it is found that the former has higher accuracy when deciding the number of inspection drones needed. Moreover, the composite reinforcement learning model performs excellently in power inspection tasks, significantly improving the efficiency of task completion.

articleTitle: Dynamic Neural Learning based Tricriteria Optimization Scheme for Dual-Redundant-Robot Manipulators Collaborative Motion Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In order to solve the optimal solution for dual redundant robot manipulators for tracking cooperative end-effector paths, a novel dynamic neural learning based tricriteria optimization (DNLTO) scheme is proposed involving multiple robot manipulators collaborative working. Specifically, the DNLTO scheme consists of two parts, i.e., tricriteria optimization scheme and DNLTO solver. To simultaneously and collaboratively control both arms, the tricriteria optimization scheme are described as left/right robot manipulators quadratic programming (QP) issues and then composed into a single QP formulation. The tricriteria optimization scheme of DNLTO scheme integrates the minimum velocity norm, repetitive motion planning, and infinity-norm velocity minimization optimization scheme through use of two weighting factors, and is reformed as standard quadratic programming problem. Then, a penalty strategy based varying-parameter recurrent neural-network is applied to solve the QP formulation. Results from computer comparisons using dual robot manipulators can verify the effectiveness and precision of the DNLTO scheme. Compare with the traditional neural network, such as a primal dual neural network with simplified linear variational inequality, the proposed DNLTO scheme has less computation time and smaller end-effector positioning errors.

articleTitle: Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion for a Dual-Ducted-Fan UAV Attitude Control under In-Ground-Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper is aimed at modeling and attitude control of a dual-ducted-fan UAV under in-ground-effect(IGE). As the UAV flies and hovers over ground or above obstacles, the IGE can cause changes in thrust/torque that drastically affects flight behavior, especially during takeoff/landing. To address this problem, the paper derives a six degree-of-freedom model of the aircraft dynamics firstly. Then, key parameters and in-ground-effect features are obtained through measurements. In order to achieve stable attitude tracking control with in-ground-effect adapting, an incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion(INDI) based cascade controller is designed. Finally, the performance of the designed INDI controller is verified by stability proof, simulations and real flight experiments.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Soft Robot Constrained Position Recognition with Multimodal Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This study initially investigates the potential issues associated with single-modality sensing in soft robotic systems and the variations in multimodal sensing weights for robot state recognition under different conditions. Subsequently, we construct a transformer-based model for the recognition of constrained states in robots and compare its performance with several alternative methods, including LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, and CNN-Att-LSTM.Experimental results show that the Transformer model outperforms methods such as LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, and CNN-Att-LSTM in terms of accuracy and reliability, with an accuracy rate of over 90% in distinguishing between constrained and unconstrained states of soft robots.

articleTitle: Water Surface Autonomus Navigation Simulation via Multi-agent Proximal Policy Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: To address the challenges of autonomous navigation and intelligent obstacle avoidance for clusters of homogeneous unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) in intricate environments, a self-driving algorithm utilizing multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is introduced. A multi-obstacle scenario is created, where the interactions among unmanned underwater vehicles are used to assess the game situation. The USV fleet undergoes training through the multi-agent proximal policy optimization algorithm (MAPPO) to facilitate autonomous driving. This approach allows for efficient route planning and effective obstacle evasion, ensuring that the vehicles reach their destination with the desired orientation and relative positioning. The simulation environment is constructed with the Unity game engine, providing visualization during training to enhance algorithm robustness. Experimental results demonstrate that both the proposed algorithm and simulation setup exhibit strong feasibility and good performance.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Direct-Discretized RNN With Fuzzy Factor for Handling Future Distinct-Layer Inequality and Equation System Applied to Robot Manipulator Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive direct-discretized recurrent neural network (ADD-RNN) algorithm with fuzzy factor to address the problem of future distinct-layer inequality and equation system (FDLIES). For comparison purposes, a traditional indirect-discretized RNN (TID-RNN) algorithm is also developed to solve the same problem. The superior performance of the proposed ADD-RNN algorithm is validated through numerical experiment. The applicability and meliority of the proposed ADD-RNN algorithm are further demonstrated by applying it to tackle a motion planning and control problem of a robot manipulator with an additional constraint, which is formulated as a specific FDLIES problem.

Author Keywords: future distinct-layer inequality and equation system (FDLIES)

articleTitle: Inductance and Core Loss Modeling and Estimation of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Subspace Learning-Based Flux Linkage Denoising
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In the field of control and optimization for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM), it is challenging to accurately estimate the inductances along the motor’s d-axis and q-axis, as well as to quantify the complex effects of core loss. This study proposes a inductance and core loss estimation method for PMSM based on flux linkage denoising and neural network modeling. Specifically, an equivalent circuit model of the PMSM considering the core loss effect is established. A noise removal technique based on subspace learning is introduced to denoise the flux linkages data. Furthermore, the flux linkage equations considering the core loss effect are integrated into the neural network to estimate the motor’s inductances and parameters related to core loss. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed neural network can accurately estimate the inductances and core loss-related parameters of PMSM, successfully addressing the issue of quantifying core loss effects, which validate effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: PLM-YOLOv5: Improved YOLOv5 for Pig Detection in Livestock Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: With the rapid development of smart agriculture, the demand for pig monitoring has been increasing, particularly in disease prevention and behavioral analysis. Real-time monitoring of pig behavior is essential for improving farming efficiency and ensuring animal welfare. However, challenges such as pigs’ varying body sizes, movement, and complex environments make accurate detection and tracking difficult. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv5 model, named PLM-YOLOv5, specifically designed for pig detection in livestock monitoring. First, we add an additional detection head to enhance the model’s capability to detect smaller pigs effectively. Next, we integrate the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to enhance feature extraction, particularly in handling complex backgrounds. Finally, we utilize a self-collected dataset of over 1,400 images for model training and validation, ensuring the model adapts to real-world livestock environments. Experimental results show that PLM-YOLOv5 achieves significant improvements in pig detection tasks, with the mean Average Precision (mAP) increasing by approximately 9% compared to the original YOLOv5. Additionally, training and validation loss curves demonstrate the model's stability and convergence. These results confirm the effectiveness and reliability of PLM-YOLOv5 for real-world applications, offering a robust solution for smart agriculture.

articleTitle: Self Balancing Performance of Wheel-legged Robots under Disturbance and Faulty Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This study investigates the self-balancing performance of a bipedal wheel-legged robot under a range of disturbances and faulty conditions. The disturbances include external kicks, additional weight loads, wind forces, trailer carrying, and collisions. Additionally, the paper evaluates the robot’s resilience under various working and fault conditions including balancing on soft and rotatable surfaces and working with wheel malfunctions. The cascaded PID and adaptive control method are employed for the robot’s balance and movement. Comprehensive simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the wheel-legged robot control.

articleTitle: Kernel Correlation Filter Algorithm and Its Research in Small Target and Occlusion Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the improvement of kernel filtering algorithms and their applications, particularly on enhancing the accuracy of target recognition and tracking in modern intelligent environmental monitoring. The Kernel Correlation Filter (KCF) algorithm, due to its efficiency, high precision, and strong robustness, holds significant potential for application in surveillance environments. However, the performance of the KCF algorithm is limited in complex scenarios such as occlusion, scale changes, similar targets, and rapid movements.To address these issues, this paper proposes two improved KCF algorithms. Firstly, a scale pool algorithm is introduced, which enhances the algorithm's adaptability to target scale changes by performing multi-scale feature extraction and matching, thereby improving tracking accuracy, efficiency, and speed. Experiments demonstrate that the tracking accuracy of the improved algorithm is significantly enhanced on the OTB50 and OTB100 datasets. In experiments using a self-constructed dataset, the success rates for feature extraction, scale changes, and sampling rates were improved by 40%, 13.6%, and 29.76%, respectively.Secondly, to address the occlusion problem, an improved joint tracking algorithm combining the modified KCF with ByteTrack is proposed. The high-quality detection results of the improved KCF are utilized as input for ByteTrack, which optimizes the handling of occluded objects through its multiple matching strategies. The joint algorithm exhibits excellent performance on the OTB50 and OTB100 datasets. In the self-constructed dataset, the success rate for handling occlusion scenarios is improved by 50% compared to the original KCF, effectively solving issues such as target template updating, feature changes, and target disappearance.

articleTitle: Automated Machine Learning-Assisted Low-Carbon Operation Optimization for Catalytic Cracking Units: A Multi-Objective Optimization Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: This study proposes a low-carbon operational optimization framework for fluid catalytic cracking (FCC) units and conducts a comprehensive evaluation of their economic performance, energy utilization, and environmental impacts. First, a low-carbon energy-saving operational optimization framework was developed to enhance the economic benefits of FCC units while exploring their carbon reduction potential. Subsequently, a surrogate-assisted model based on an automated machine learning (AutoML) framework was constructed to reduce computational costs. A carbon tax scenario was then introduced, converting CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions into carbon tax values. This approach can improve the computational efficiency of the multi-objective optimization problem. The experimental results demonstrate that optimizing operational conditions increased unit-time profits by 0.5%, reduced CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions by 1088.92 kgCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>eq/h, and decreased wind energy and steam energy consumption by 627.67 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h and 324.28 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/h, respectively. The scientific optimization of operational parameters enhances production efficiency while mitigating environmental impacts, providing valuable guidance for energy conservation and emissions reduction in industrial processes and supporting sustainable development.

articleTitle: Optimization of Control Laws for Performance Maintenance of Turboshaft Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Automatic Control (IRAC)
abstract: In order to address the issue of engine performance degradation resulting from component deterioration during the operational lifespan of turboshaft engines, this paper conducts an in-depth study on the analysis of turboshaft engine performance degradation and the optimization of performance maintenance control strategies. Firstly, utilizing the component-level model of the turboshaft engine, the study investigates the impact of various online controllable parameters, including the adjustable guide vane angle of the compressor, the gas generator speed, and the power turbine speed, on the overall engine performance. Subsequently, an optimized control strategy for the combination of these online controllable parameters is devised. The primary objective of this strategy is to ensure that the total temperature at the power turbine inlet remains within safe limits, that the gas generator speed and power turbine speed do not exceed their respective maximum rpm values, while simultaneously maintaining the engine's output power. The effectiveness of this control strategy is rigorously verified through simulation. The simulation results demonstrate that the optimized control strategy is capable of effectively sustaining the turboshaft engine's output power during emergency conditions, resulting in a remarkable extension of engine life by 111.4%.
